newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dlr ends weak, plagued by NY selling, Peters.
newsitem.headline: NZ dlr ends weak, plagued by NY selling, Peters.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar ended the week in poor style on Friday, plagued by a hangover from New York selling overnight and some surprising comments on the likely shape of the 1997/98 budget next week.
The kiwi closed the local session at US$0.6856/66 against its 0.6870/77 open and 0.6875/80 close on Thursday, and dealers expected it to trade lower over the weekend.

Treasurer Winston Peters, speaking after giving a speech to an Auckland business lunch meeting, said he felt market observers had too optimistic a view of the country's fiscal prospects ahead of next week's budget.
Asked if financial markets had been too complacent about the fiscal outlook, Peters told Reuters, "I think they have been considerably too optimistic".
He gave a clear signal that budget surpluses would be smaller than previously indicated and the government's borrowing requirement larger than it was last year.

"I think after that a few who had been sitting a touch long (in kiwi) took advantage to sell some. We saw some selling from Tokyo, some out of Australia, and overall it's just got a very heavy feel to it," one dealer said.
